title: IPC → BNS 2023, CrPC → BNSS, BSA; medical law (negligence, consent, MTP, PCPNDT, THOA, MHCA)
subject: Forensic Medicine
anchor: BNS, BNSS and BSA 2023 replaced IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act from 1 July 2024: questions now quote the NEW section numbers.
Murder 302 → BNS 103 | culpable homicide 299/304 → 100/105 | death by negligence 304A → 106 | dowry death 304B → 80 | rape 375/376 → 63/64
Hurt 319/323 → 114/115 | grievous hurt 320/325 → 116/117 | acid attack 326A/B → 124 | consent 87–92 → 25–30
Inquest CrPC 174 → BNSS 194 | rape victim exam 164A → BNSS 184 | dying declaration IEA 32(1) → BSA 26

tables.title: IPC → BNS 2023 (medically relevant)
head: Offence / provision
IPC
BNS 2023
rows: Child below 7 yr: nothing is an offence
Act of person of unsound mind (McNaughten rule)
Consent: act not intended/known to cause death or GH (≥18 yr)
Consent in good faith for person's benefit (e.g., surgery)
Guardian's consent for child <12 yr / unsound mind
Consent under fear / misconception / by child/insane is not consent
Act done in good faith without consent (emergency)
Rape causing death / persistent vegetative state
Assault to outrage modesty of woman
Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
Death by rash/negligent act (incl. medical negligence)
Acid attack / attempt to throw acid
Not retained as a general offence (BNS 226 only punishes attempted suicide to compel/restrain a public servant)

tables.title: CrPC → BNSS 2023 and Evidence Act → BSA 2023
head: Provision
Old
New
rows: Police inquest (report to magistrate within 24 h in BNSS)
Magistrate inquest (custodial death, dowry death <7 yr of marriage, rape in custody)
Medical exam of accused at request of police
Medical exam of arrested person (on his request)
Recording of confession / statement by magistrate
Medical exam of rape victim (consent; report to IO within 7 days)
Free treatment of victims of acid attack / rape by all hospitals
Dying declaration (relevance of statement of dead person)
Presumption of absence of consent in rape

points: **BNS 106(1)**: death by negligence = up to 5 yr; proviso for a **registered medical practitioner** during a medical procedure = up to **2 yr** + fine. 106(2) = hit-and-run.
**Bolam test (1957, UK)**: a doctor is not negligent if he acted in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by a responsible body of medical opinion.

**Jacob Mathew v State of Punjab (SC 2005)**: criminal liability needs **gross** negligence/recklessness; private complaint must be backed by credible opinion of another competent doctor before prosecution.
**V.P. Shantha (SC 1995)**: medical services (paid) fall under the Consumer Protection Act. Res ipsa loquitur = 'the thing speaks for itself' (e.g., swab left in abdomen).

**MTP (Amendment) Act 2021**: ≤20 wk → opinion of 1 RMP; 20–24 wk → 2 RMPs, only for special categories (rape survivors, minors, change of marital status, disability etc.); >24 wk only for substantial fetal anomalies on Medical Board opinion; contraceptive-failure ground extended to 'any woman or her partner'.
**PCPNDT Act 1994** (renamed 2003): bans sex selection and disclosure of fetal sex; all USG machines must be registered; Form F maintained for every prenatal USG.

**THOA 1994 (THOTA amendment 2011)**: brainstem death certified by a board of 4 (incl. RMP in charge, neurologist/neurosurgeon, an RMP nominated by the authority, and the medical administrator); tests done twice, ≥6 h apart; organ trade punishable.

**Mental Healthcare Act 2017**: S.115 presumes severe stress in attempted suicide (no prosecution); advance directive & nominated representative; ECT only with anaesthesia + muscle relaxant; ECT not for minors except with board permission.

Consent types: implied (attending OPD), expressed – oral/written; **informed consent** for any procedure with risk; blanket consent is not valid. Age of valid consent for harm (BNS 25) = **18 yr**; guardian consent below 12 yr (BNS 27).

traps.stem: A surgeon is charged after a patient dies due to an anaesthetic mishap. Under which BNS section is he tried and what is the maximum term for a registered medical practitioner?
traps.trap: BNS 105 / IPC 304 (culpable homicide) — tempting because death followed an act, but no intention/knowledge.
traps.fix: BNS 106(1) (old IPC 304A): death by rash/negligent act; for an RMP during a medical procedure, up to 2 years + fine. Criminal liability requires gross negligence (Jacob Mathew).

traps.stem: A 19-year-old survives a suicide attempt. Can she be prosecuted under the new code?
traps.trap: Yes, under 'BNS equivalent of IPC 309' — many assume every IPC section was renumbered.
traps.fix: No. BNS has no general offence of attempted suicide; MHCA 2017 S.115 already presumed severe stress. Only BNS 226 (attempt to suicide to compel/restrain a public servant) survives.

traps.stem: Section of the new law under which police hold an inquest in an unnatural death?
traps.trap: BNSS 174 — reflexively carrying over the CrPC number.
traps.fix: BNSS 194 (old CrPC 174). Magistrate inquest = BNSS 196 (old 176). India has no coroner system now.

cards.text: Murder: IPC 302 → BNS {{c1::103}}; death by negligence IPC 304A → BNS {{c2::106}}; dowry death IPC 304B → BNS {{c3::80}}.
Rape: IPC 375/376 → BNS {{c1::63/64}}; acid attack IPC 326A → BNS {{c2::124}}.

cards.front: Police inquest and magistrate inquest — BNSS sections?
cards.back: Police inquest BNSS 194 (old CrPC 174); magistrate inquest BNSS 196 (old CrPC 176).

cards.front: MTP Amendment 2021: gestational limits and number of RMPs?
cards.back:
≤20 wk: 1 RMP
20–24 wk: 2 RMPs (special categories only)
>24 wk: substantial fetal anomaly, Medical Board
Criminal prosecution of doctor needs gross negligence; complaint must be supported by credible opinion of another competent doctor.

cards.text: IPC consent sections 87–92 map to BNS {{c1::25–30}}; valid consent to risk of harm requires age ≥ {{c2::18}} years.

verify: BNS/BNSS/BSA 2023 (in force 1 July 2024); MTP Amendment 2021; MHCA 2017. Older answer keys may still quote IPC/CrPC numbers — learn both.

title: Mechanical injuries & firearm wounds (ballistics)
subject: Forensic Medicine
anchor: Lacerated wound = irregular bruised margins + tissue bridges; incised = clean margins, length > depth; stab = depth > length.
Entry wound: small, inverted, abrasion collar + grease collar; skull entry bevels the INNER table, exit bevels the OUTER table.
Contact = muzzle imprint, gas splitting (stellate over bone), soot in track, cherry-red CO; tattooing (stippling) = unburnt powder at intermediate range, cannot be wiped off.
Contre-coup: moving head strikes a fixed object → contusion opposite the impact (frontal/temporal poles on occipital fall).

tables.title: Firearm wound by range (rifled handgun, approximate)
head: Range
Features
rows: Muzzle imprint abrasion; soot and gases driven into the track; stellate/cruciate split over bone (scalp); cherry-red tissue from CO; no tattooing on skin
Burning/singeing of skin & hair, blackening (soot, wipeable), tattooing; flame zone ~ few cm
Tattooing/stippling only (powder grains embedded, NOT wipeable); blackening absent beyond ~ 30 cm
Only the bullet hole with abrasion + grease collar; cannot estimate exact range

tables.title: Wound discriminators
head: Feature
Lacerated
Incised
Stab
rows: Clean; one or both ends acute
Over bone (scalp, shin) it looks incised: split laceration

points: **Contusion colour**: red (fresh) → blue (hours–3 d) → bluish-black/brown (haemosiderin, ~4 d) → **green (biliverdin, 5–6 d)** → **yellow (bilirubin, 7–12 d)** → normal by ~2 wk. Deep bruises appear late and away from the site (ectopic bruise, e.g., spectacle haematoma).
**Abrasion**: no scab/bright red when fresh; reddish scab 12–24 h; brown scab 2–3 d; scab falls ~ 7–10 d. Patterned abrasion identifies the object (tyre, ligature, nail).
**Rifled firearm**: lands and grooves → spin → accuracy; single bullet; rifling marks used to match bullet to weapon. **Smoothbore (shotgun)**: no rifling, fires pellets.

**Choke** = constriction of the shotgun barrel at the muzzle → keeps pellets together longer. **Rule of thumb**: spread of shot (inches) ≈ range (yards); single hole at very close range, 'rat-hole' with scalloped margin as pellets begin to spread, then satellite pellet holes.

**Dum-dum** (expanding, soft/hollow nose) → large wounds; **tandem bullet** = two bullets, one entry; **keyhole/tumbling** bullet → oval or irregular entry; **Kennedy phenomenon** = surgical alteration of a wound; **souvenir bullet** = retained bullet encapsulated.
**Shored exit**: exit wound with an abrasion collar because skin was supported (belt, wall).
**Blast**: primary (pressure wave) hits air-containing organs: **TM rupture is commonest**, **blast lung** commonest fatal; secondary = fragments; tertiary = body thrown; quaternary = burns/toxic.

Skull fractures: **ring fracture** around foramen magnum (fall on feet/buttocks); **hinge (motorcyclist's) fracture** across middle cranial fossae; **pond** fracture in infants; **signature** (depressed) fracture reproduces weapon shape; **gutter** fracture (tangential bullet).
Extradural haematoma: middle meningeal artery, lucid interval; subdural: bridging veins, commonest in elderly/infants (shaken baby).

traps.stem: A scalp wound from a blunt rod has straight, sharp-looking margins. How do you call it?
traps.trap: Incised wound — margins look clean because skin is split against underlying bone.
traps.fix: Split laceration: look for tissue bridges, crushed hair bulbs and abraded/bruised margins in the depth.

traps.stem: Blackening around a firearm entry wound washes off with a wet swab, but the speckled pattern remains. Which feature remains and what does it indicate?
traps.trap: Blackening — tempting because both are dark marks around the wound.
traps.fix: Tattooing/stippling (unburnt powder embedded in the skin) remains; blackening = soot, wipeable. Tattooing indicates close-to-intermediate range, not distant.

traps.stem: Bevelling found on the outer table of a skull defect — entry or exit?
traps.trap: Entry — 'the bullet hits the outside first'.
traps.fix: Exit. The cone opens in the direction of travel: entry bevels the inner table, exit bevels the outer table.

cards.text: Contusion turns {{c1::green}} at 5–6 days (biliverdin) and {{c2::yellow}} at 7–12 days (bilirubin).

cards.front: Wipeable vs non-wipeable powder marks around a gunshot wound?
cards.back: Blackening (soot) is wipeable; tattooing/stippling (embedded unburnt powder) is not.

cards.front: Skull bevelling at entry vs exit?
cards.back: Entry: inner table bevelled. Exit: outer table bevelled.

cards.text: Choke is the constriction at the muzzle of a {{c1::shotgun (smoothbore)}} barrel; it {{c2::reduces dispersion}} of pellets.

cards.front: Most common organ injured by primary blast? Most common fatal?
cards.back: Tympanic membrane rupture (commonest); blast lung (commonest fatal).

cards.text: Fall on the buttocks or feet transmits force through the spine to cause a {{c1::ring}} fracture of the skull base around the foramen magnum.

images.commons: File:Experimental gunshot entrance wound - dist to target 0 inch.jpg
images.caption: Contact-range entrance (.38 revolver, Glessner Lee test plate): soot and gas effects are confined to the wound and its edge, with no wide tattooing ring

images.commons: File:Experimental gunshot entrance wound - dist to target 1 inch.jpg
images.caption: Close range (1 inch): central entry hole surrounded by blackening and powder tattooing — the zone widens and becomes fainter as the range increases

verify: Ranges are approximate and weapon-dependent (Reddy / Narayan Reddy FMT). Do not memorise a single exact cm cut-off.

title: Thanatology: postmortem changes & time since death
subject: Forensic Medicine
anchor: Algor → livor → rigor → decomposition; livor fixes ~6–8 h; rigor follows Nysten's order (heart first, then eyelids/jaw … fingers & toes last).
Cherry-red lividity = CO; bright red/pink = cyanide and cold; chocolate/brown = methaemoglobin (nitrites, chlorates, aniline).
Cadaveric spasm = instant, localised, ante-mortem act (weapon gripped) — cannot be simulated; heat stiffening = pugilistic attitude, protein coagulation.
Vitreous potassium rises steadily after death = best chemical marker of PMI.

tables.title: Hypostasis vs bruise; spasm vs rigor
head: Feature
Postmortem lividity
Bruise (contusion)
rows: Dependent parts, spares pressure areas (contact pallor)
Any site, at point of impact
Blood extravasated into tissues, does not wash away

algorithm:
Body found → estimate time since death
  Temperature: PMI (h) ≈ (normal − rectal temp in °F) ÷ 1.5 (exam-classic; sigmoid curve, initial plateau)
  Lividity: appears ~1 h, well developed ~4 h, FIXED ~6–8 h (does not shift on turning)
  Rigor: appears 1–2 h, full ~12 h, persists ~12 h, passes off ~12 h (temperate; faster in Indian summer)
  Eyes: tache noire (scleral blackening) in a few hours if eyes open; Kevorkian sign (segmented retinal blood) within minutes
  Decomposition: green discolouration right iliac fossa (caecum) ~12–18 h in summer → marbling → bloating/frothy fluid
  Chemistry: vitreous K⁺ rises linearly (best) ; CSF/blood values unreliable
  Late: insects (entomology), adipocere (moist) or mummification (dry)
points: **Algor mortis**: postmortem caloricity (temperature rises after death) in heat stroke, tetanus, strychnine, septicaemia, cholera, pontine haemorrhage.

**Rigor mortis** = ATP depletion → actin–myosin cross-bridges fixed. **Nysten's law**: myocardium first; then eyelids, face/jaw, neck, upper limbs, trunk, lower limbs; fingers/toes last; passes off in the same order.

**Cadaveric spasm** (instantaneous rigor): no primary flaccidity, single group of muscles, ante-mortem act; e.g., weapon grasped in suicide, weeds/grass clutched in drowning — proof of the act at the moment of death.
**Heat stiffening** > 65 °C → protein coagulation → **pugilistic attitude** (not proof of fighting). **Cold stiffening** = freezing of body fluids/fat.

Earliest external sign of putrefaction = **greenish discolouration of the right iliac fossa** (caecum, H₂S + sulphmethaemoglobin). Among the earliest internal organs: larynx/trachea mucosa; **non-gravid uterus and prostate** are among the last.

**Adipocere (saponification)**: hydrolysis + hydrogenation of body fat into fatty acids; needs warm moist conditions; aided by Clostridium perfringens lecithinase; preserves features → identification.
**Mummification**: desiccation in hot dry air with free air movement; skin leathery, brown; features preserved.
**Maceration**: sterile autolysis of a fetus dead in utero (≥ 24 h); skin slippage, rancid smell — sign of intrauterine death (not putrefaction).

**Autopsy techniques**: Virchow — organs removed one by one; Rokitansky — in-situ dissection; Letulle — en masse; Ghon — en bloc (organ systems). I-shaped incision is commonest; Y/modified-Y preferred for detailed neck dissection.
**Exhumation** ordered by an executive (District/Sub-divisional) magistrate; India has no time limit.

traps.stem: Hypostasis on the back of a corpse does not shift on turning the body prone. Interpretation?
traps.trap: Death < 2 h ago — confusing 'appearance' with 'fixation'.
traps.fix: Lividity is fixed (≈6–8 h after death). If lividity is seen over both back and front, the body was moved after partial fixation.

traps.stem: A dead man's hand tightly grips a revolver. Rigor mortis elsewhere is absent. What does this show?
traps.trap: Rigor mortis — early rigor of the hand.
traps.fix: Cadaveric spasm: instantaneous, localised, cannot be produced after death → indicates the weapon was held at death (suggests suicide).

traps.stem: Burnt body with flexed limbs in a boxer's posture — sign of an ante-mortem fight?
traps.trap: Yes, defensive posture.
traps.fix: No. Heat stiffening (pugilistic attitude) from coagulation of muscle proteins occurs whether burnt alive or after death.

cards.text: Postmortem lividity becomes fixed about {{c1::6–8}} hours after death; CO poisoning gives a {{c2::cherry red}} colour.

cards.back: Myocardium first; then eyelids → face/jaw → neck → upper limbs → trunk → lower limbs → fingers & toes last; passes off in the same order.

cards.front: Cadaveric spasm vs rigor mortis — 3 differences?
cards.back: Spasm: instantaneous (no primary flaccidity), localised, ante-mortem act, cannot be simulated. Rigor: after 1–2 h of flaccidity, generalised, follows Nysten's order.

cards.text: Earliest external sign of putrefaction is greenish discolouration of the {{c1::right iliac fossa}}; best chemical marker of time since death is {{c2::vitreous potassium}}.

cards.back: Adipocere: warm, moist (hydrolysis + hydrogenation of fat). Mummification: hot, dry, ventilated (desiccation).

cards.front: Autopsy technique where organs are removed one by one?
cards.back: Virchow. (Rokitansky in situ; Letulle en masse; Ghon en bloc.)

images.caption: Postmortem lividity: purplish discolouration in dependent parts with pale contact areas where the body pressed on the surface

verify: Timings are Indian textbook averages (Reddy); they vary with climate. Exam-classic temperature formula uses °F.

title: Asphyxial deaths, identification, sexual offences & infanticide
subject: Forensic Medicine
anchor: Hanging = oblique, incomplete ligature mark ABOVE thyroid, pale hard parchment base; salivary dribble = ante-mortem hanging.
Strangulation = horizontal, complete, at/below thyroid, soft and bruised; thyroid/cricoid fractures; usually homicidal.
Drowning: fine persistent froth, weeds clutched (cadaveric spasm), Paltauf haemorrhages; diatoms in femoral bone marrow = most reliable.
Gustafson (teeth) for adult age; pelvis best for sex; hydrostatic test = respiration after birth.

tables.title: Hanging vs ligature strangulation
head: Feature
Hanging
Ligature strangulation
rows: Hyoid/thyroid fracture uncommon; carotid intimal tears
Thyroid cartilage/cricoid fracture common; deep bruising
Throttling: crescentic nail marks, hyoid fracture

points: **Le facies sympathique**: eye on the side of the knot open with dilated pupil (cervical sympathetic pressure) → ante-mortem hanging. Typical hanging = knot at the occiput.

**Burking** = smothering + traumatic asphyxia (kneeling on chest); **mugging** = arm-lock strangulation; **bansdola** = bamboo across neck; **garrotting** = ligature from behind; **café coronary** = food bolus in larynx.
**Traumatic asphyxia**: chest compression (crowd crush) → craniofacial congestion, petechiae, subconjunctival haemorrhage (masque ecchymotique).

**Drowning**: fresh water → haemodilution, haemolysis, hyperkalaemia, VF within minutes; sea water → haemoconcentration and pulmonary oedema (slower). **Emphysema aquosum** (water-logged lungs). **Dry drowning** = laryngospasm. **Washerwoman's hands** = immersion only, not proof of drowning. Gettler chloride test is unreliable.

**Gustafson's criteria** (adult age from teeth): attrition, periodontosis, secondary dentine, cementum apposition, root resorption, **root transparency (most reliable)**. Boyde: incremental enamel lines (neonatal line).

**Sex**: pelvis most reliable bone (wide sciatic notch, subpubic angle > 90°, preauricular sulcus, ischiopubic index > 90 in female), then skull. **Stature**: Karl Pearson / Trotter–Gleser formulae; femur best long bone.

**Dactylography** (Galton, Henry classification): loops commonest, arches least; prints are unique even in identical twins. **Poroscopy** (Locard) = sweat pores; **cheiloscopy** = lip prints; **rugoscopy** = palatal rugae.
**DNA fingerprinting** (Alec Jeffreys): VNTR/STR; mitochondrial DNA (maternal) for degraded remains/hair shaft; Y-STR for male lineage. Best sample from skeletonised remains: teeth (pulp)/bone.

**Sexual offences**: rape = BNS 63/64; POCSO 2012 for < 18 yr (mandatory reporting); **two-finger test banned** (SC Lillu 2013, reaffirmed 2022); exam needs victim's consent (BNSS 184), report to IO within 7 days; free treatment mandatory (BNSS 397).

**Infanticide**: **hydrostatic test** (lungs float = respiration; false + in putrefaction/artificial respiration); **Breslau's second life test** = air in stomach/intestine; **Ploucquet's** = lung weight ratio (≈1/70 before, ≈1/35 after respiration). **Spalding sign** = overlapping skull bones in IUD. **Haase's rule**: fetal length (cm) = months² up to 5 months, then months × 5.

traps.stem: Neck shows a horizontal, continuous ligature mark below the thyroid cartilage in a body found suspended. Diagnosis?
traps.trap: Hanging — because the body was found hanging.
traps.fix: Strangulation followed by suspension (homicide staged as suicide). Mark level, direction and continuity decide, not the scene.

traps.stem: Most reliable test to confirm ante-mortem drowning in a decomposed body?
traps.trap: Gettler's chloride test or froth at mouth — classic but unreliable/lost with decomposition.
traps.fix: Diatom test on bone marrow of long bones (femur): diatoms reach marrow only with a functioning circulation.

traps.stem: Floating lungs in a newborn found in a drain — proof of live birth?
traps.trap: Yes — hydrostatic test positive.
traps.fix: Not if putrefied (gas floats lungs) or after artificial respiration. Test is invalid in decomposition; corroborate with stomach-bowel test and histology.

cards.text: Most reliable sign of ante-mortem hanging is {{c1::salivary dribbling}}; ligature mark in hanging is {{c2::oblique and non-continuous}}.

cards.front: Most reliable Gustafson criterion for age?
cards.back: Root transparency (dentine sclerosis).
Large, pale bluish-red subpleural haemorrhages (haemolysed) under the visceral pleura in drowning.

cards.text: Breslau's second life test looks for {{c1::air in stomach and intestines}}; the {{c2::hydrostatic}} test looks for lungs floating.

cards.back: Loops commonest; arches least common.

cards.text: Haase's rule: fetal length in cm = {{c1::months squared}} for the first 5 months and {{c2::months × 5}} thereafter.

verify: Sexual-offence provisions per BNS/BNSS 2023 and POCSO 2012; SC ban on two-finger test (2013, 2022).

title: Toxicology quick table: metals, gases, plant & animal poisons
subject: Forensic Medicine
anchor: Lead: Burton line + basophilic stippling + wrist drop + colic. Arsenic: Mees lines, raindrop pigmentation, rice-water stools, body preserved.
Cyanide: bitter almonds, bright red lividity, fastest killer (cytochrome oxidase). CO: cherry red, COHb, globus pallidus necrosis.
Datura: dry as a bone, red as a beet, blind as a bat, mad as a hatter, hot as a hare → physostigmine.
Locard's exchange principle: every contact leaves a trace.

tables.title: Poisons: key features and antidotes
head: Poison
Discriminating features
Treatment / antidote
rows: Acute: rice-water stools (mimics cholera), red velvety gastric mucosa; chronic: Mees lines, raindrop pigmentation, hyperkeratosis, neuropathy; detected in hair/nails; resists putrefaction
Burton blue gum line, basophilic stippling, ↑urinary ALA & coproporphyrin (ALA dehydratase + ferrochelatase blocked), wrist/foot drop, colic, encephalopathy in children
CaNa₂EDTA; succimer (DMSA) oral; BAL + EDTA in encephalopathy
Inorganic: erethism, hatter's/Danbury tremors, acrodynia (pink disease) in children; methyl mercury: Minamata disease
BAL (inorganic), DMSA; avoid BAL in methylmercury
Bitter almond smell, bright red lividity, rapid death; blocks cytochrome oxidase (complex IV)
Cherry-red skin/lividity; Hb affinity ~ 200–250× O₂; bilateral globus pallidus necrosis; delayed neuropsychiatric sequelae
Anticholinergic: dry, flushed, mydriasis, hyperthermia, delirium (picking at bedclothes); kidney-shaped flat yellow-brown seeds; road poisoning by thugs
Euphoria, hallucinations, increased appetite; 'run amok'; Duquenois–Levine test
Muscarinic (SLUDGE, miosis, bronchorrhoea), nicotinic (fasciculation), kerosene smell; ↓ RBC cholinesterase; intermediate syndrome
Atropine to drying of secretions + pralidoxime (early)
Bright red seeds with black spot; abrin (toxalbumin) – crushed seeds made into needles (sui) for cattle poisoning
Cardiac glycosides (thevetin): vomiting, bradycardia, heart block, hyperkalaemia – digoxin-like
Aconitine (Na⁺ channel opener): tingling & numbness of mouth then body, VT/VF; root mistaken for horseradish
Elapids (cobra, common krait) – neurotoxic, ptosis, descending paralysis; krait bite painless, nocturnal, abdominal pain. Vipers (Russell's, saw-scaled) – haemotoxic, coagulopathy (20WBCT), AKI
Polyvalent ASV; neostigmine + atropine for cobra (post-synaptic) paralysis

points: **Basophilic stippling** of RBCs: lead poisoning (classic), also thalassaemia, sideroblastic anaemia.

**Viscera preservation**: saturated common salt solution; **rectified spirit** for viscera except in poisoning by alcohol, kerosene, phenol, phosphorus, paraldehyde, acetic acid. Blood for alcohol: **sodium fluoride** (+ potassium oxalate).

Viscera for chemical analysis: stomach + contents, small intestine (30 cm) + contents, liver (~500 g), half of each kidney; blood ~ 10 mL; urine ~ 30 mL. Hair/nails for chronic arsenic and other metals.
**Locard's exchange principle**: perpetrator leaves and takes away trace evidence (fibres, hair, soil) — basis of trace evidence; Locard also founded poroscopy.
**Marsh / Reinsch tests** detect arsenic; **Duquenois–Levine** test = cannabis.
**Universal antidote** (historical): activated charcoal 2 parts + MgO 1 + tannic acid 1 — now obsolete; activated charcoal alone is used.
**Methyl alcohol**: formic acid → optic neuritis/blindness, wide anion gap acidosis → fomepizole or ethanol, haemodialysis.
**Paraquat**: lung fibrosis (do not give O₂ liberally); **aluminium phosphide** (celphos): phosphine gas, garlic odour, refractory shock, silver nitrate paper turns black.

traps.stem: Child with anaemia, abdominal colic, wrist drop and blue line on gums. Smear finding?
traps.trap: Ring sideroblasts only — tempting because lead causes sideroblastic picture.
traps.fix: Coarse basophilic stippling (inhibition of pyrimidine 5′-nucleotidase); Burton line clinches lead. Treat with CaNa₂EDTA/succimer.

traps.stem: Victim of house fire with bright cherry-red lividity — cause?
traps.trap: Cyanide — fires also release HCN and both give red lividity.
traps.fix: Cherry-red is classic for CO (COHb); cyanide gives bright red/brick red. Fire victims may have both; measure COHb.

traps.stem: Viscera from a suspected phenol poisoning case — which preservative?
traps.trap: Rectified spirit — the 'routine' preservative.
traps.fix: Saturated common salt solution; rectified spirit is avoided in alcohol, kerosene, phenol, phosphorus, paraldehyde and acetic acid poisoning.

cards.front: Burton line + basophilic stippling + wrist drop — poison and chelator?
cards.back: Lead. CaNa₂EDTA (± BAL in encephalopathy); oral succimer (DMSA) in children.

cards.text: Mees lines and raindrop pigmentation indicate chronic {{c1::arsenic}} poisoning; antidote {{c2::BAL (dimercaprol)}}.

cards.back: Inhibits cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) → histotoxic hypoxia. Hydroxocobalamin (alternative: nitrites + sodium thiosulphate).

cards.text: Datura poisoning is treated with {{c1::physostigmine}}; its seeds are {{c2::kidney-shaped, flat, yellowish-brown}}.

cards.back: Every contact leaves a trace: the offender both leaves and carries away material — basis of trace evidence.

cards.text: Blood sample for alcohol estimation is preserved with {{c1::sodium fluoride}}.

images.caption: Basophilic stippling: blue granules (aggregated ribosomes) in RBCs — classic in lead poisoning (pyrimidine 5′-nucleotidase inhibition)

verify: Antidotes per Harrison 21e / KD Tripathi; viscera preservation per Reddy FMT.

title: Biostatistics: 2×2 table, risk measures, distributions & tests of significance
subject: Community Medicine
anchor: Sensitivity = a/(a+c) (SnNout); specificity = d/(b+d) (SpPin); PPV = a/(a+b); NPV = d/(c+d).
Sens & spec are properties of the test; PPV ↑ and NPV ↓ as prevalence ↑.
Cohort → RR, AR; case-control → OR; NNT = 1/ARR.
Normal curve: ±1 SD 68%, ±2 SD 95% (exactly ±1.96), ±3 SD 99.7%; mean = median = mode.

tables.title: 2×2 table and derived measures (a = TP, b = FP, c = FN, d = TN)
head: Measure
Formula
Note
rows: High sensitivity rules OUT (SnNout); best for screening
High specificity rules IN (SpPin); best for confirmation
ARR = CER − EER; RRR = ARR / CER; NNT = 1 / ARR

algorithm:
Worked NNT example
  Control event rate (CER) = 20%; experimental event rate (EER) = 15%
  ARR = 20 − 15 = 5% = 0.05 → NNT = 1/0.05 = 20
  RRR = 0.05/0.20 = 25%; RR = 0.15/0.20 = 0.75
PPV vs prevalence (sens 90%, spec 90%, 1000 people)
  Prevalence 10%: TP 90, FP 90 → PPV 50%
  Prevalence 50%: TP 450, FP 50 → PPV 90%
points: **Mean** affected by extreme values; **median** best for skewed data; **mode** for nominal data. Positive skew: mean > median > mode.

**Dispersion**: range (simplest), mean deviation, **SD** (most useful), variance = SD²; **coefficient of variation** = SD/mean × 100 (compare variability of different units). **Standard error** of mean = SD/√n.
**Type I (α) error** = rejecting a true null (false positive); α usually 0.05. **Type II (β)** = accepting a false null (false negative). **Power** = 1 − β (usually 80%).
**p-value** = probability of the observed (or more extreme) result if null hypothesis is true; not the probability that H₀ is true.
**95% CI** = mean ± 1.96 SE; CI for a ratio (RR/OR) crossing 1, or for a difference crossing 0 = not significant.
**Sample size** increases with smaller α, higher power, smaller detectable difference, larger variability.

Scales: nominal (sex, blood group), ordinal (staging, Likert), interval (°C), ratio (weight, true zero). Histogram for continuous; bar chart for discrete; pie chart for proportions; scatter for correlation; ogive = cumulative frequency; frequency polygon.
**Correlation coefficient** r ranges −1 to +1; **r²** = coefficient of determination; regression predicts y from x.
Normal distribution: bell-shaped, symmetric, mean = median = mode, total area = 1; **Z score** = (x − mean)/SD.

traps.stem: A test is used in a population where disease prevalence falls. What happens to sensitivity, specificity and PPV?
traps.trap: Sensitivity falls — confusing test properties with predictive values.
traps.fix: Sensitivity and specificity are unchanged; PPV falls and NPV rises as prevalence falls.

traps.stem: Blood pressure measured in the same 30 patients before and after a drug. Test?
traps.trap: Unpaired t-test — two sets of means.
traps.fix: Paired t-test (same subjects). Non-normal data → Wilcoxon signed-rank.

traps.stem: Case-control study of smoking and lung cancer. Which measure of association?
traps.trap: Relative risk — the familiar 'risk' term.
traps.fix: Odds ratio (ad/bc). Incidence cannot be calculated in case-control design, so RR and AR need a cohort.

cards.text: Sensitivity = {{c1::a/(a+c)}}; PPV = {{c2::a/(a+b)}}; PPV {{c3::rises}} with prevalence.
In a normal distribution, mean ± {{c1::1.96}} SD covers 95% of values and ± 3 SD covers {{c2::99.7%}}.

cards.front: Non-parametric equivalents of unpaired t, paired t and ANOVA?
cards.back: Mann–Whitney U; Wilcoxon signed-rank; Kruskal–Wallis.

cards.text: Type I error = {{c1::rejecting a true null hypothesis (false positive)}}; power = {{c2::1 − β}}.

cards.back: Sensitivity ÷ (1 − specificity).

title: Screening, study designs, bias & epidemic investigation
subject: Community Medicine
anchor: Series testing → ↑ specificity; parallel testing → ↑ sensitivity.
Lead-time bias = earlier diagnosis inflates survival; length-time bias = screening picks slow-growing disease; overdiagnosis = disease that would never cause harm.
Point-source epidemic: single sharp peak, all cases within one incubation period; propagated: successive peaks one incubation period apart.
SAR = (cases among contacts within one IP) ÷ susceptible contacts; herd immunity threshold = 1 − 1/R₀.

tables.title: Study designs
head: Design
Direction / unit
Measure
Key bias / feature
rows: Recall bias, Berkson (admission-rate) bias; good for rare disease
Loss to follow-up (attrition); good for rare exposure
Gold standard; randomisation removes known & unknown confounders

tables.title: Phases of clinical trials
head: Phase
Subjects
Purpose
rows: Confirm efficacy & safety vs standard → licensing

points: **Wilson–Jungner (WHO 1968)** screening criteria: important health problem, recognisable latent/early stage, natural history understood, suitable and acceptable test, accepted treatment, facilities available, agreed policy on whom to treat, cost-effective, continuous process.
**ROC curve**: sensitivity (y) vs 1 − specificity (x); best cut-off nearest the top-left corner; **AUC** = overall accuracy (0.5 = useless, 1 = perfect).

**Bias** types: selection, information/measurement (recall, interviewer), confounding. **Hawthorne effect** = behaviour changes when observed. **Berkson** = hospital-based case-control. **Healthy worker effect** in occupational cohorts.
**Confounder**: associated with both exposure and outcome, not on the causal pathway. Control: randomisation, restriction, matching (design); stratification, multivariate analysis (analysis).
**Blinding**: single (subject), double (subject + investigator), triple (+ analyst). **Allocation concealment** prevents selection bias; blinding prevents measurement bias.
**Intention-to-treat analysis** preserves randomisation. **Cross-over** and **cluster** RCTs; **non-randomised** = natural experiments.
**Incubation period**: time from infection to first symptom; use **median** IP; serial interval = onset in primary to onset in secondary case.
**SAR**: measles ~80% (highly infectious). Denominator excludes the primary case and immune contacts.
**Herd immunity threshold** = 1 − 1/R₀ (measles R₀ ~ 12–18 → ~ 92–95% coverage needed).
**Bradford Hill** criteria for causation: temporality (only essential one), strength, consistency, specificity, biological gradient, plausibility, coherence, experiment, analogy.

traps.stem: Two tests are applied one after the other and only those positive on both are labelled positive. Effect?
traps.trap: Sensitivity increases — 'two tests are better'.
traps.fix: Series (sequential) testing raises specificity and PPV, lowers sensitivity. Parallel testing (positive on either) raises sensitivity.

traps.stem: Screening programme shows 5-year survival rose from 40% to 60% but mortality rate is unchanged. Explanation?
traps.trap: Screening is effective.
traps.fix: Lead-time bias (and length-time bias/overdiagnosis). The proper end-point for screening is disease-specific mortality in an RCT.

traps.stem: Food-poisoning outbreak: all cases occur within 12 hours after a wedding lunch. Type of epidemic curve?
traps.trap: Propagated epidemic — many cases in a short time.
traps.fix: Common-source, single-exposure (point-source) epidemic: one sharp peak, all cases within one incubation period, no secondary waves.

cards.text: Series testing increases {{c1::specificity}}; parallel testing increases {{c2::sensitivity}}.

cards.back: Y: sensitivity (TPR). X: 1 − specificity (FPR). AUC = overall accuracy.

cards.front: Measure of association in case-control vs cohort?
cards.back: Case-control: odds ratio. Cohort: relative risk and attributable risk.

cards.text: Herd immunity threshold = {{c1::1 − 1/R₀}}.

cards.back: Temporality (cause must precede effect).
Post-marketing surveillance in the general population to detect rare/long-term ADRs.

images.commons: File:Epidemic curve of Hepatitis A Nov-Dec 1978.jpg
images.caption: Common-source outbreak: index case, then a steep rise and fall of cases within about one incubation period, with a few secondary cases trailing
Propagated (person-to-person) epidemic: successive peaks separated by roughly one incubation period

title: National programmes: UIP schedule, cold chain, NTEP, malaria, leprosy, NACP, RMNCH+A
subject: Community Medicine
anchor: UIP: 6-10-14 wk = OPV + Pentavalent + Rota; fIPV at 6 & 14 wk (+ 9 mo); PCV 6 wk, 14 wk, booster 9 mo; MR at 9–12 & 16–24 mo; Td at 10 & 16 yr.
VVM: inner square lighter than outer circle = use; square matches or is darker = discard.
NTEP: NAAT upfront; new DS-TB = 2HRZE + 4HRE daily FDC by weight band.
Malaria: P. vivax = chloroquine 3 d + primaquine 0.25 mg/kg × 14 d; P. falciparum = ACT (AS+SP; AL in North-East) + single-dose primaquine.

tables.title: Universal Immunization Programme (India)
head: Age
Vaccines
rows: BCG, OPV-0, Hepatitis B birth dose (within 24 h)
MR-1, JE-1 (endemic districts), PCV booster, fIPV-3, Vitamin A 1st dose (1 lakh IU)
MR-2, JE-2, DPT booster-1, OPV booster, Vitamin A 2nd dose (2 lakh IU), then every 6 months till 5 yr (9 doses)
Td-1 early, Td-2 four weeks later; one Td booster if vaccinated within the previous 3 years

tables.title: Vaccine vial monitor (heat exposure)
head: Stage
Appearance
Action
rows: Inner square much lighter than outer circle
Square still lighter than circle but darker than stage 1
Square same colour as circle (discard point)

points: **Cold chain**: ILR and walk-in cooler +2 to +8 °C; deep freezer and walk-in freezer −15 to −25 °C (OPV storage at higher levels, ice-packs). **OPV** most heat-sensitive; **Hep B, Penta, DPT, Td, IPV, PCV** freeze-sensitive (**shake test** for suspected freezing). Reconstituted **BCG, MR, JE** discarded after 4 h or session end.
**Open vial policy**: opened multi-dose vials of OPV, Penta, DPT, Td, Hep B, IPV, PCV may be used up to 28 days if VVM usable, not expired, cold chain kept, no contamination.
**U-WIN**: digital registry (Co-WIN model) recording every vaccination of pregnant women and children up to 16 yr; e-certificates and due reminders.
**Mission Indradhanush (Dec 2014)**: catch-up for un/partially immunised children and pregnant women; target ≥90% full immunisation; Intensified MI (IMI) rounds since 2017.

**NTEP**: Ni-kshay portal; **Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana** DBT for nutrition of every notified TB patient (₹500/month, enhanced to ₹1000/month in 2024 — verify). TB-free target: 2025 (SDG 2030). TPT: 3HP or 6H for contacts/PLHIV. MDR/RR-TB: all-oral shorter bedaquiline regimen; 6-month **BPaLM** (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) introduced.
**DS-TB weight bands (adult FDC: H75 R150 Z400 E275)**: 25–34 kg = 2 tablets; 35–49 kg = 3; 50–64 kg = 4; 65–75 kg = 5; > 75 kg = 6.

**Malaria (NCVBDC)**: API = confirmed cases/year per 1000 population; ABER target ≥ 10%. Severe malaria: IV artesunate. Primaquine contraindicated in pregnancy, infants and G6PD deficiency. 1st-trimester P. falciparum: quinine (national guideline).

**Leprosy (NLEP)**: PB = 1–5 lesions, ≤1 nerve, smear −ve (6 months); MB = ≥6 lesions or >1 nerve or smear +ve (12 months). Adult MB monthly: rifampicin 600 + clofazimine 300; daily clofazimine 50 + dapsone 100. India moved PB patients to the 3-drug regimen (2025) — verify. Contacts: single-dose rifampicin PEP.
**NACP-V (2021–26)**: 95-95-95; test-and-treat; first-line ART **TLD** (tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir).

**JSY (2005)** cash incentive for institutional delivery; **JSSK (2011)** free delivery incl. caesarean, drugs, diagnostics, diet, blood, transport (home–facility–home) for pregnant women and sick infants. **RMNCH+A (2013)** continuum of care. **Ayushman Bharat (2018)**: HWCs (now Ayushman Arogya Mandirs) with expanded primary care packages + PM-JAY ₹5 lakh/family/year.

traps.stem: VVM on an OPV vial: inner square the same colour as the outer circle. Use?
traps.trap: Use — 'not yet darker than circle'.
traps.fix: Discard. Stage 3 (square = circle) is the discard point; use only if the square is lighter.

traps.stem: Which vaccine is damaged by freezing and should be checked by the shake test?
traps.trap: OPV — the most heat-sensitive vaccine is assumed most temperature-sensitive overall.
traps.fix: Adsorbed (aluminium) vaccines: Hep B, Pentavalent, DPT, Td (also IPV, PCV) are freeze-sensitive; OPV can be frozen.

traps.stem: Adult with new pulmonary TB in India: continuation phase?
traps.trap: 4HR (classic international regimen).
traps.fix: NTEP uses 4HRE (ethambutol continued) — 2HRZE + 4HRE daily FDC by weight band.

cards.text: Under UIP, PCV is given at {{c1::6 weeks, 14 weeks and 9 months (booster)}} and Td at {{c2::10 and 16}} years.

cards.front: VVM stages to use vs discard?
cards.back: Stage 1–2 (square lighter than circle): use (stage 2 first). Stage 3–4 (square equal/darker): discard.

cards.text: ILR temperature range is {{c1::+2 to +8 °C}}; the most heat-sensitive vaccine is {{c2::OPV}}.

cards.front: NTEP regimen for new drug-sensitive TB?
cards.back: 2HRZE + 4HRE, daily fixed-dose combination by weight band.
Chloroquine 25 mg/kg over 3 days + primaquine 0.25 mg/kg daily × 14 days (avoid in pregnancy, infants, G6PD deficiency).

cards.text: Leprosy MB: ≥ {{c1::6}} skin lesions or > 1 nerve or smear positive; treated for {{c2::12}} months.

verify: MoHFW UIP schedule (fIPV-3 at 9 mo added 2023); NTEP 2024 guidelines; NCVBDC malaria drug policy. Ni-kshay Poshan amount and PB leprosy 3-drug change are recent — confirm against latest notification.

title: Biomedical waste, water & air, vector control, occupational health
subject: Community Medicine
anchor: BMW 2016: Yellow = anatomical/soiled/incinerable; Red = contaminated recyclable plastics; White translucent = sharps; Blue = glassware & metallic implants.
Chlorination: residual free chlorine 0.5 mg/L after 1 h contact; Horrock's apparatus = bleaching powder dose for a well; orthotolidine test = residual chlorine.
Silicosis = eggshell calcification + TB; asbestosis = lower lobe + pleural plaques + mesothelioma; byssinosis = Monday tightness (cotton).
Temephos (Abate) 1 ppm in drinking water; Paris green = anopheline larvicide; Gambusia/guppy = larvivorous fish.

tables.title: Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016 (amended 2018)
head: Colour
Waste
Treatment / disposal
rows: Human/animal anatomical waste, soiled waste (dressings, plaster, cotton with blood), expired/discarded medicines, chemical waste, discarded linen, pre-treated microbiology/lab waste; cytotoxic drugs (with cytotoxic label)
Incineration / plasma pyrolysis / deep burial (where permitted)
Contaminated recyclable waste: tubing, bottles, IV sets, catheters, urine bags, syringes without needles, gloves
Autoclave / microwave / hydroclave → shredding → recycling (never incinerated)
Waste sharps incl. metals: needles, syringes with fixed needles, scalpel blades
Autoclave / dry heat sterilisation → shredding / encapsulation / sharps pit

tables.title: Pneumoconioses and organic dust diseases
head: Disease
Dust / agent
Discriminator
rows: Most dangerous; upper-lobe nodules, eggshell calcification of hilar nodes, ↑ TB risk
Progressive massive fibrosis; Caplan syndrome with RA
Lower-lobe fibrosis, pleural plaques, asbestos (ferruginous) bodies, mesothelioma, lung cancer (synergy with smoking)
Chest tightness on first day of work week (Monday fever)

points: **Chlorine demand** = chlorine used up by organic matter; **breakpoint chlorination** = point where demand is met and free residual chlorine appears. Bleaching powder has ~33% available chlorine.
**Orthotolidine (OT) test** measures free + combined chlorine; **OT-arsenite** test separates free from combined and corrects interference.
**Horrock's apparatus**: 6 white cups + 2 black cups; starch–iodide indicator; first cup showing blue gives the dose of bleaching powder for 455 L (100 gallons) of water.

**Bacteriological quality**: coliforms as indicator; **presumptive coliform test** (multiple-tube, MacConkey broth, MPN per 100 mL); E. coli (thermotolerant) must be absent in any 100 mL of drinking water. **Slow sand filter**: vital layer (Schmutzdecke) = biological; rapid sand filter needs alum coagulation.

**NAAQS 2009 (CPCB)**: PM2.5 annual 40, 24 h 60 µg/m³; PM10 annual 60, 24 h 100 µg/m³. **National AQI (2014)**: 8 pollutants; categories Good 0–50, Satisfactory 51–100, Moderate 101–200, Poor 201–300, Very poor 301–400, Severe 401–500.

**Mosquito features**: Anopheles — rests at an angle, eggs with lateral floats, larva parallel to water (no siphon); Culex — egg rafts, larva with siphon hangs at angle; Aedes — black-white striped, day biter, breeds in artificial containers; Mansonia — larvae attach to roots of Pistia (remove Pistia).
**Aedes indices**: house index, container index, **Breteau index** (positive containers per 100 houses — best for density).

**ESI Act 1948**: wage ceiling ₹21,000/month; contribution employer 3.25%, employee 0.75%; benefits — medical, sickness (~70% of wages up to 91 days), maternity (26 weeks full wages), disablement, dependants', funeral, unemployment allowance.

**Noise**: permissible occupational limit 85–90 dB(A) for 8 h; noise-induced hearing loss first at **4000 Hz** (notch). Lead, benzene (aplastic anaemia/AML), vinyl chloride (hepatic angiosarcoma), aniline dyes/β-naphthylamine (bladder cancer).

traps.stem: Used IV set and urine bag (no needles) — which bin?
traps.trap: Yellow — 'infected waste goes to yellow'.
traps.fix: Red: contaminated recyclable plastics, autoclaved/shredded and recycled; never incinerated.

traps.stem: Broken contaminated glass ampoules and a removed orthopaedic metal implant — bin?
traps.trap: White sharps container — because they are sharp/metallic.
traps.fix: Blue cardboard box: glassware and metallic body implants. White translucent is for needles, blades and other waste sharps.

traps.stem: Acceptable residual chlorine after chlorination of drinking water?
traps.trap: 0.5 mg/L immediately after adding chlorine.
traps.fix: Free residual 0.5 mg/L at the END of 1 hour contact time (the contact period matters).

cards.text: BMW 2016: needles and blades go into the {{c1::white translucent puncture-proof}} container; glassware and metallic implants into the {{c2::blue}} box.
Recommended free residual chlorine is {{c1::0.5 mg/L}} after a contact period of {{c2::1 hour}}.

cards.back: To estimate the dose of bleaching powder needed to disinfect well water (starch–iodide end-point).

cards.front: Eggshell calcification of hilar nodes + increased TB risk?
cards.back: Silicosis.

cards.text: Noise-induced hearing loss first appears at {{c1::4000 Hz}}.

cards.back: Number of Aedes-positive containers per 100 houses inspected.

verify: BMW Management Rules 2016 (2018 amendment); CPCB NAAQS 2009; ESI rates as revised July 2019.

title: Demography indicators, socioeconomic scales & nutrition programmes
subject: Community Medicine
anchor: IMR, NMR, U5MR use live births as denominator; maternal mortality RATIO per 1,00,000 live births vs maternal mortality RATE per 1,00,000 women 15–49.
NRR = 1 ≈ TFR 2.1 = replacement level; India NFHS-5 TFR = 2.0.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat 6×6×6; pregnant women = 1 IFA (60 mg iron + 500 µg FA) daily from 2nd trimester for 180 days.
Lathyrism = BOAA (khesari dal); epidemic dropsy = sanguinarine (argemone oil).

tables.title: Demographic & mortality indicators
head: Indicator
Numerator
Denominator (×)
rows: Stillbirths (≥ 28 wk) + early neonatal deaths (first 7 days)
Daughters a newborn girl will bear, allowing for mortality

points: **Demographic cycle (5 stages)**: high stationary → early expanding → **late expanding (India)** → low stationary → declining.
Headline values (verify latest): NFHS-5 (2019–21) **TFR 2.0**, sex ratio (total population) 1020 F/1000 M; SRS 2018–20 MMR **97**/1,00,000 live births.
**Maternal death** = death during pregnancy or within 42 days of termination, from any cause related to/aggravated by pregnancy, not accidental. Late maternal death = 42 days–1 yr.

**Modified Kuppuswamy** (urban): education + occupation + monthly family income → 5 classes; **B.G. Prasad** (urban & rural): per-capita monthly income. Income cut-offs of both are **updated with CPI (Industrial Workers)** — do not memorise fixed rupee values. **Pareek** scale for rural.
**ICMR-NIN 2020**: reference adult man 65 kg, woman 55 kg; introduces EAR alongside RDA.
**Vitamin A prophylaxis**: 1 lakh IU at 9 months, then 2 lakh IU every 6 months to 5 yr (9 doses). Xerophthalmia treatment: 2 lakh IU on days 0, 1, 14 (half dose 6–12 months).

**Anaemia Mukt Bharat IFA**: 6–59 mo 1 mL syrup (20 mg Fe + 100 µg FA) biweekly; 5–9 yr 45 mg Fe + 400 µg FA (pink) weekly; 10–19 yr 60 mg + 500 µg (blue) weekly; WRA 60 mg + 500 µg (red) weekly; pregnancy & lactation 60 mg + 500 µg (red) daily ×180 days each. Deworming albendazole biannually.

**Food adulterants**: argemone oil in mustard oil → epidemic dropsy (sanguinarine; nitric acid test); Lathyrus sativus → neurolathyrism (BOAA), spastic paraplegia; aflatoxin (Aspergillus flavus, groundnuts) → hepatocellular carcinoma; Claviceps (ergot); Crotalaria/pyrrolizidine alkaloids → endemic ascites (veno-occlusive disease); metanil yellow in turmeric/sweets.

**ICDS (1975)**: 6 services — supplementary nutrition, immunisation, health check-up, referral, pre-school education, nutrition & health education; children < 6 yr, pregnant & lactating women, adolescent girls. Supplementary nutrition: children 500 kcal + 12–15 g protein; severely underweight 800 kcal + 20–25 g; pregnant/lactating 600 kcal + 18–20 g.
**POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018)** → Mission Poshan 2.0; **PM POSHAN** (mid-day meal): primary 450 kcal + 12 g protein, upper primary 700 kcal + 20 g protein.

traps.stem: Denominator of maternal mortality ratio?
traps.trap: Women of reproductive age — that is the maternal mortality RATE.
traps.fix: Ratio = maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births (India's SRS figure); rate uses women 15–49 yr.

traps.stem: Replacement-level fertility corresponds to which value?
traps.trap: TFR = 1 or GRR = 1.
traps.fix: NRR = 1 (≈ TFR 2.1). NRR accounts for female mortality before reproductive age.

traps.stem: A family with paralysis of both legs after eating a cheap pulse during drought. Toxin?
traps.trap: Argemone oil/sanguinarine — another adulterant toxin.
traps.fix: Lathyrism: BOAA in khesari dal (Lathyrus sativus) → spastic paraplegia. Argemone causes epidemic dropsy (oedema, glaucoma).

cards.text: Perinatal mortality rate = (stillbirths + {{c1::early neonatal deaths in first week}}) per 1000 {{c2::live births + stillbirths}}.

cards.back: Replacement level fertility: each woman replaced by exactly one daughter (≈ TFR 2.1).

cards.text: Anaemia Mukt Bharat: pregnant women take one tablet with {{c1::60 mg elemental iron + 500 µg folic acid}} daily for {{c2::180 days}}.

cards.back: Sanguinarine in argemone oil; nitric acid test (or paper chromatography).
Supplementary nutrition, immunisation, health check-up, referral, pre-school non-formal education, nutrition & health education.

cards.text: India is in the {{c1::late expanding}} stage of the demographic cycle.

verify: SRS 2018–20 MMR 97 and NFHS-5 (2019–21); newer SRS bulletins may update values. ICDS norms revised 2017; Anaemia Mukt Bharat 2018.

title: Prevention levels, communicable disease epidemiology & surveillance (IDSP)
subject: Community Medicine
anchor: Primordial = prevent emergence of risk factors; primary = health promotion + specific protection; secondary = early diagnosis & treatment (screening); tertiary = disability limitation + rehabilitation; quaternary = protect from overmedicalisation.
Rabies category III (transdermal bite, licks on broken skin, mucosal contact, bat) = wound wash + vaccine + RIG.
IDSP forms: S (syndromic, health worker), P (presumptive, doctor), L (laboratory confirmed); now on IHIP.
Outbreak: verify diagnosis → confirm epidemic → case definition & case search → time/place/person → hypothesis → test → control → report.

tables.title: Disease-specific epidemiology (high-yield facts)
head: Disease
Key epidemiological facts
rows: SAR ~80%; IP ~10 days to fever (≈14 to rash); infectious 4 days before to 4 days after rash; no carriers; MR elimination goal

Mostly inapparent infection; AFP surveillance in < 15 yr (non-polio AFP rate ≥ 2/1,00,000 target in India), 2 stool samples 24 h apart within 14 days of onset; India certified polio-free 2014 (last wild case Jan 2011)
IP hours to 5 days; El Tor: more carriers & inapparent infections; O139 Bengal; ORS + doxycycline/azithromycin
Chronic carriers (> 1 yr) harbour in gallbladder; Vi antibody for carrier detection; typhoid conjugate vaccine from 6 months

Cat I: touching/licks on intact skin → no PEP. Cat II: nibbling, minor scratch without bleeding → wound wash + vaccine. Cat III: transdermal bite/scratch, licks on broken skin/mucosa, bats → wash + vaccine + RIG
Aedes aegypti (day biter, artificial containers); NS1 antigen in first 5 days, IgM after day 5; warning signs → critical phase
Culex tritaeniorhynchus; pigs = amplifier hosts; ardeid birds = reservoir; man = dead-end host; live SA-14-14-2 vaccine
Long IP (years); droplet from nasal discharge of untreated MB patients main source; children = index of active transmission
Window period before antibodies; mother-to-child transmission prevented by lifelong ART + infant prophylaxis

points: **Epidemiological triad**: agent, host, environment; **web of causation** for chronic disease (MacMahon).
**Modes of intervention** (Leavell & Clark): health promotion, specific protection (immunisation, iodised salt), early diagnosis & treatment, disability limitation, rehabilitation.
**Primordial prevention** example: preventing adoption of smoking/unhealthy diet in children; **specific protection** example: immunisation, chemoprophylaxis, helmets.
**Rabies vaccine schedules**: IM Essen 0, 3, 7, 14, 28 (5 doses); ID Updated Thai Red Cross 2-2-2-0-2 (days 0, 3, 7, 28). Pre-exposed persons: 2 boosters (days 0, 3), no RIG.

**Carrier** = infected without symptoms who sheds the agent (incubatory, convalescent, healthy; temporary or chronic). Carriers are more dangerous than cases for spread of typhoid, diphtheria, polio, cholera.

**Surveillance**: passive (routine reports) vs active (health workers seek cases, e.g., malaria house visits); **sentinel** (selected sites, e.g., HIV); **IDSP (2004)** decentralised, lab-supported; **IHIP** real-time digital platform.
**Iceberg phenomenon**: hidden mass of undiagnosed/subclinical cases (e.g., hypertension, diabetes, polio). Disease with no iceberg: rabies, measles (almost all clinical).
**Isolation** period depends on period of communicability; **quarantine** (for contacts) = longest incubation period of the disease.
**Eradication**: smallpox (1980); elimination = reduction to zero/below threshold in a region (India: polio-free 2014, maternal & neonatal tetanus eliminated 2015, yaws-free 2016).

traps.stem: Child licked by a stray dog on an abrasion on the forearm. Category and management?
traps.trap: Category II — because it was 'only a lick'.
traps.fix: Lick on broken skin = Category III: wound wash + anti-rabies vaccine + rabies immunoglobulin.

traps.stem: Advice to teenagers in a school not to start smoking — which level of prevention?
traps.trap: Primary prevention — health education is listed under health promotion.
traps.fix: Primordial prevention: preventing the emergence of the risk factor itself in a population where it has not yet appeared.

traps.stem: Quarantine duration for contacts of a disease?
traps.trap: Period of communicability — that governs isolation of cases.
traps.fix: Quarantine = longest incubation period of the disease (applies to healthy contacts).

cards.text: Disability limitation and rehabilitation are {{c1::tertiary}} prevention; screening is {{c2::secondary}} prevention.

cards.back: Single/multiple transdermal bites or scratches, licks on broken skin, mucosal contamination with saliva, bat exposure → wash + vaccine + RIG.

cards.front: IDSP S, P and L forms?
cards.back: S = syndromic (health worker); P = presumptive (clinician); L = laboratory-confirmed.

cards.text: In JE, pigs are {{c1::amplifier hosts}} and man is a {{c2::dead-end host}}; vector is Culex tritaeniorhynchus.
Quarantine lasts for the {{c1::longest incubation period}} of the disease.

cards.back: About 80% among susceptible household contacts.

verify: Park PSM 27e; National Guidelines for Rabies Prophylaxis (NRCP 2019).
